cards.explanation: The answer is a boat. The crowds got so large that Jesus got into a boat and sat down, while all the people stood on the shore (Matthew 13:2). I think that's a pretty smart spot to teach from, friends. Crowd on the shore, Jesus in the boat.
The answer is birds. Some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it (Matthew 13:4). Seed just lying out on a path is easy pickings, friends. Nobody had to sneak in, either.

The answer is False. The seed on rocky ground sprang up quickly, and the text says it was because the soil was shallow (Matthew 13:5). Not much soil, not much waiting, friends. That little seedling was in a hurry.

The answer is True. Jesus says that when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched (Matthew 13:6). That seed had sprung up quickly because the soil was shallow (Matthew 13:5). Then the sun rose and it did not go well, friends.

The answer is that they had no root. Jesus says the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root (Matthew 13:6). I've seen cookies that looked great on the tray and fell apart when I picked them up, so I get it, bakers. Something was missing underneath.

The answer is choke. Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings (Matthew 13:7). The thorns were not sitting there politely, friends. They grew up right alongside the seed and crowded it out.

The answer is up to a hundred times over, friends. The seed on good soil produced a crop, and Jesus gives three amounts: a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold (Matthew 13:8). Even the smallest number there is thirty times what was sown. After three rough patches, this ending is a big one.

The answer is that they ask why He speaks to the people in parables. The disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why do You speak to the people in parables?” (Matthew 13:10). They were not asking about the farmer or the seed, friends. They wanted to know why Jesus teaches this way.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.” (Matthew 13:11). He is talking to the disciples there, friends. The word “given” tells me this knowledge came as a gift to them.

The answer is that it will be taken away. Jesus says, “Whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” (Matthew 13:12). It's the other half of the line about whoever has being given more, friends. That one is heavy, so it deserves a slow read.

The answer is that they do not truly see or understand. Jesus says, “Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.” (Matthew 13:13). He then quotes Isaiah, who says they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes (Matthew 13:15). So the reason, friends, is that they do not see or understand.

The answer is closed. Jesus quotes Isaiah, the prophet, saying, “they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes.” (Matthew 13:15). So the picture, friends, is hearts gone callous, ears that hardly hear, and eyes that are shut.

The answer is True. The prophecy says, “Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.” (Matthew 13:15). So it names seeing, hearing, understanding and turning, and then healing. That's a door left open, friends.

The answer is that they are blessed because they see and hear. Jesus tells His disciples, “But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.” (Matthew 13:16). After talking about eyes that don't see, He turns to the ones that do. I think that's good news after a heavy stretch, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says many prophets and righteous men “…longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.” (Matthew 13:17). They longed for it, friends. The disciples are the ones who get to see and hear it.

The answer is the evil one. Jesus says, “…the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the seed sown along the path.” (Matthew 13:19). It's about someone who hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it, friends. What was sown in his heart gets snatched away.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “The seed sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.” (Matthew 13:20). So the start is happy and it's quick, friends. The trouble comes in the next verse.

The answer is falls away. Jesus says, “But since he has no root, he remains for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he quickly falls away.” (Matthew 13:21). No root means he lasts only a season, friends. The joy was real, but there was nothing below holding it.

The answer is unfruitful. Jesus says the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, “…and it becomes unfruitful.” (Matthew 13:22). Choking is the picture here, friends. The worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth do the crowding.

The answer is that he understands it. Jesus says, “But the seed sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it.” (Matthew 13:23). Hearing is only the start, friends. This one hears, understands, and bears fruit.
